subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should #41824 stay plugin/ClawHub claim-verifier scope using existing hooks, or should OpenClaw core add a narrow runId/delivery-correlation seam for reliable Telegram/source-channel verifier plugins?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans Telegram delivery, agent runtime state, and optional policy enforcement; #68051 already scoped broad claim verification to plugins, but current outbound hook docs still show a possible exact-turn correlation gap.

options.title: Keep Verifier Policy In Plugins
options.body: Core should avoid a built-in claim verifier and only accept a narrow hook/correlation fix if a plugin proof shows the current API cannot gate exact turns reliably.

options.title: Add A Narrow Core Seam
options.body: Core should plumb run/delivery correlation through outbound hooks and leave the verifier implementation itself to a plugin.

options.title: Promote Core Claim Verification
options.body: Core should own a built-in side-effect claim ledger and warn/strict delivery behavior despite the new compatibility-sensitive policy surface.

recommendation.title: Keep Verifier Policy In Plugins
recommendation.body: Core should avoid a built-in claim verifier and only accept a narrow hook/correlation fix if a plugin proof shows the current API cannot gate exact turns reliably.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete made the closest recorded product-boundary decision on #68051 and is the strongest owner signal for plugin scope versus core policy.
